It was late to discuss only why there were only 12 people and so on and so forth. It was important that we got some people back. They crossed the line of separation, nobody was firing, and this exchange was carried out properly. Later, it was established that none of the people on the list, this additional list of 40 people, were on this list. These people who did come were from other municipalities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did this take place, if you can just give us a date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The action was on the 12th of June. I can't be precise, but it was five or six days after the 12th of June, so it could have been the 7th or the 8th of June. I can't say exactly, but five or six days later, anyway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I understand correctly, initially it was denied that there were any detainees, but eventually, actually, there were people from Karakaj that were taken out and exchanged against the three bodies; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right. Later on, when we talked to the people, those 12 people, of whom one was from Divic, Zvornik municipality, we later learnt -- well, they told us the names of the people whom they had been in contact with, or they tried to remember their surnames. So we learnt it was a ruse, a trick, and that there were many, many people who were executed in the technical school centre or in some of the other camps that I've mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you maintain a copy, or did you also have a copy of the list of about 250 people, yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I kept a copy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you very briefly tell us, what did you do with that copy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That photocopy and some other documents about the civilian organisation, or organising the civilian population for defence when they were leaving the territory, the territory that I was living in, on the 1st of February, 1993, I buried that. I buried it in a house or, rather, in a space where there was supposed to be a toilet built. I put them in a nylon bag and a leather -- a bigger leather bag. And after I gave my statement in 1996, in the month of August, in Tuzla, I told the investigators about these documents. And after that, they organised a visit for me to the Orao base of UNPROFOR in Tuzla on the 11th of October, 1996, and I went to the house where I had buried those documents. I dug them up, handed them over to the investigators, whether it was The Hague Tribunal or whatever at the time, anyway, to the investigators, I handed over all those documents, and they took them away, dried them. And when we next met -- well, some of them had been destroyed, but others not.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. I don't remember, Judges, that I ever received any of those documents. Perhaps I did, but could the Prosecutor then tell me when, and where, and if I did .

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: The accused did not receive a copy of those, and efforts are being made also at this very moment to identify the documents. But I'd like to show a document to the accused, and I have copies for the -- sorry, a copy of a document to the witness and also provide copies to everyone else in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is -- what is this list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This list was -- this list was compiled by the leadership, the people in charge of dealing with the civilian population in my area, of taking care of them. It was personally written by one of my assistants or associates. We compiled this on the basis of information that we received from people who were there, who were present, who lived through those war days in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me interrupt you, because we only have five minutes left. This particular copy, I can see there's something written in English on it. Who -- do you know who have written on it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I remember, this was written by a woman called Marija. She from Slovenia, and she worked for that institution at the time, to the best of my recollections. Whether I got it right, I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This particular copy, did you provide that to the Office of the Prosecutor yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This specific copy, well, I had it in my documents and I provided it yesterday. I had a list of 250 people who had been taken prisoner.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, we can make further submissions on this, but in very brief, my understanding of what has happened is that the Prosecution's copy that was originally provided by the accused has been destroyed as part of a clean-up of evidence which it was unsafe to keep, so the Prosecution has not been able to locate a copy of the documents that the witness originally gave to us. The witness was, in 2002, given a copy of what he had given us, and he brought this document with him when he came to The Hague. We would request leave to amend our exhibit list to add this document to our exhibit list, and I would seek the admission of this particular document. What I would propose in practice, if Your Honours agree to admit --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: If Your Honours agree to admit the exhibit, I would suggest that we ask the witness for his copy, and we have a proper scan made that we can put into evidence. The relevance of this exhibit is, of course, it's a contemporaneous record of what the witness was told about who were detained at Karakaj, and I would draw Your Honours' attention, for example, to numbers 27 and 28 on the list. And as we're not showing the list, I think I can safely say that one of these people has been a witness in this case and another one is his father. So, Your Honours, this is a bit unusual, but I do think it's significant, and I can provide further records of what had happened to the OTP's copy of this material. But the bottom line is that today this is the best version of the list that we have, and I think it's significant, and we seek its admission. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, what do you have to say to this?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you can see, Judges, what the Prosecutor has just told us, if I understood him correctly. The Prosecution received this document several years ago, and then they destroyed it. And then yesterday the witness brought another copy of that document to them, and now they want to tender it into evidence by the back door. I think that that is absolutely impermissible. First of all, it's illegible. Somebody wrote some comments on it in English. We don't know who did that. There's no date, there's no reference as to location. All it says here is that it is a list of captured persons, and asking for the exchange. That's what it says in the title. So the Muslim side is exchanging their own people for others. Who, on the part of the Muslims? How? We know nothing. The witness brought this in yesterday, and he doesn't know who wrote these comments on the document in English, either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, please give us the copy you have, your copy. Hand it over to the usher, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your own copy. I want your copy, the one you have in your file. I would like to look at the quality of the document. As regards the photocopy, the first page is legible, but the other pages are difficult to read.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, my understanding from our record is that the documents were very damaged when they were received. Efforts were made to dry them, and basically what you see is the poor state of the documents. If I may make a response to the objection. The witness is here to give details about the compilation of this and establish the reliability of what is typed on the document, so if there are any questions about how the list came about, those questions can be put to the witness. We only seek the admission of this for the purpose of the list of names, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber, after having deliberated, decides to admit this document. Can we have an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is Exhibit P831, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, please take this document, and a copy will be given to the witness. The Registry will keep this copy, and you have another copy of your document. Fine. So we have an exhibit number for it, and the Trial Chamber feels that we have enough information that this document may have probative value and that this document may show reliable indicia, and this document is relevant. Mr. Marcussen, your time is just about up. Did you have any other questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will waive my remainder of time for direct examination and -- in order to facilitate this process, so I will not put any further questions. I may have some in redirect, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Seselj, tomorrow you will have two hours for your cross-examination. You have the entire evening to prepare yourself, since you have the document in question. You may put questions about this document; I don't know. Tomorrow, we --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand you at all, Mr. President. You mean on the basis of this document, that I should prepare on the basis of this document? That's absolutely impossible. If you mean on the basis of the DVD, once again, absolutely impossible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Whatever the case may be, you have two hours for your cross-examination tomorrow. You told us that this witness was important. I assume you have already prepared your cross-examination of this witness. We shall meet again. Witness, you must contact no one. You are a protected witness. You must not contact anyone. We shall meet again tomorrow at a quarter past 2.00. I wish you a pleasant evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 5th day of February, 2009, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.05 p.m.,
